title: Tensorization above the first moment
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space, and let $p,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1\le p$, $1<q$, and $0\le\rho\le1$. Suppose that for every coordinate $i$ and every real-valued function $g$ on that coordinate, the function $x\mapsto \rho g(x)+(1-\rho)\mathbb E_i g$ has $q$-moment norm at most the $p$-moment norm of $g$, with respect to the coordinate weights of $P$. Then every real-valued function $f$ on the product outcome space satisfies $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le \|f\|_{p,P}$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to one
The stated one-coordinate norm inequality holds for every coordinate and every real-valued coordinate function
$f$ is a real-valued function on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $p\ge1$, $q>1$, and $0\le\rho\le1$. If every coordinate probability law satisfies $\|\rho g+(1-\rho)\mathbb E_i g\|_{q,i}\le\|g\|_{p,i}$ for every real $g$ on that coordinate, then $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{p,P}$ for every $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\|g\|_{p,i}=(\sum_{a\in\Omega_i}w_i(a)|g(a)|^p)^{1/p}$ and $\mathbb E_i g=\sum_{a\in\Omega_i}w_i(a)g(a)$, where $w_i$ gives the probability masses in coordinate $i$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
